coverage.note: W6 translation of the guide. Every guide id and every translatable prose field is covered; ids and structural fields stay exactly as guide.json declares them.

sisyphus.funcion: Orchestrator that plans, decides exploration, and delegates across agents and category-with-skills combos.
sisyphus.cuandoUsar: Lead orchestrator: plans with todos, decides when to explore, and splits work across agents and models. Use it to drive a whole task from start to finish.

hephaestus.funcion: Autonomous deep worker that executes goals with GPT Codex.
hephaestus.cuandoUsar: Autonomous goal-oriented worker that executes with GPT Codex. Use it for deep work when a provider with a supported GPT model is connected; otherwise it is dropped from the roster.

prometheus.funcion: Builds the work plan, with a strict plan format.
prometheus.cuandoUsar: Plan builder: turns a goal into a verified work plan. Use it before execution when the task is broad or ambiguous.

oracle.funcion: Read-only consultant for hard debugging and architecture design.
oracle.cuandoUsar: Read-only consultant for high-difficulty reasoning: hard debugging and architecture design. Use it when a problem resists or you must choose between alternatives.

librarian.funcion: Researches external code and docs: remote repositories and official documentation.
librarian.cuandoUsar: External code researcher: reads remote repositories, retrieves official documentation, and finds usage examples. Use it to understand someone else's library or pattern.

explore.funcion: Contextual searcher of the codebase: locates where each thing is.
explore.cuandoUsar: Contextual search inside the codebase: answers where something is and which file implements it. Fire several in parallel to map an unfamiliar module.

multimodal-looker.funcion: Reads PDFs, images and diagrams that are not plain text.
multimodal-looker.cuandoUsar: Interpreter of non-text material: PDFs, images and diagrams. Use it when the detail lives in a file that is not plain text.

metis.funcion: Pre-planning analyst: hidden intentions, ambiguities and foreseeable failures.
metis.cuandoUsar: Pre-planning consultant: spots hidden intentions, ambiguities and the points where AI usually fails. Use it before planning something complex.

momus.funcion: Plan reviewer: judges clarity, verifiability and completeness.
momus.cuandoUsar: Plan reviewer: judges clarity, verifiability and completeness. Use it to challenge a plan before executing it.

atlas.funcion: Executor that walks the pending task list and completes it.
atlas.cuandoUsar: Plan executor: walks the pending task list and completes each item until done. Use it to empty an already written plan.

sisyphus-junior.funcion: Focused executor with no delegation, same discipline as Sisyphus.
sisyphus-junior.cuandoUsar: Focused executor: the same discipline as Sisyphus but with no delegation. Use it for one bounded unit of work.

judge.funcion: Independent adversarial acceptance auditor (separate beta layer).
judge.cuandoUsar: Independent adversarial acceptance auditor: verifies finished work with evidence and returns APPROVED, REJECTED or BLOCKED, without implementing fixes. Use it only when you explicitly ask to judge, audit or test something.

ast-grep.funcion: Searches and rewrites code by shape (AST) across 25 languages.
ast-grep.uso: Use it when the target is a syntactic pattern (every call shaped a certain way, a codemod), not literal text.

browser.funcion: Drives a real browser from the JavaScript evaluation kernel.
browser.uso: Use it for sites you are signed into, forms, JS-rendered pages, screenshots and web QA.

coding-agent-sessions.funcion: Finds, reads and reconstructs local coding-agent sessions.
coding-agent-sessions.uso: Use it to search past conversations, transcripts or runs and recover what an earlier session did.

data-scientist.funcion: Processes and analyzes data with resident engines (DuckDB, Polars).
data-scientist.uso: Use it for CSV, parquet or JSON, grouping, time series, cleaning or plots.

debugging.funcion: Runs a hypothesis-driven debugging loop in any language or binary.
debugging.uso: Use it for hangs, silent failures, wrong responses, memory leaks or reverse engineering.

frontend.funcion: Builds, styles and polishes web UI and UX.
frontend.uso: Use it for any page, component, layout, animation or visual-quality task.

git-master.funcion: Handles git work: atomic commits, rebase, squash, blame, bisect and reflog.
git-master.uso: Use it when a commit or a history investigation is needed; not for ordinary code edits.

init-deep.funcion: Initializes a hierarchical AGENTS.md knowledge base for a project.
init-deep.uso: Use it when a repository needs its structure, commands and conventions documented for agents.

lsp-setup.funcion: Configures a language server for editor and agent tooling.
lsp-setup.uso: Use it when a project needs an LSP or the no-LSP-server notice appears.

programming.funcion: Applies strict modern practice (typed errors, exhaustive match, tests that can fail) in Python, Rust, TypeScript and Go.
programming.uso: Use it when working on .py, .rs, .ts or .go files.

refactor.funcion: Guides a refactor, cleanup or restructure with the right decomposition.
refactor.uso: Use it when asked to refactor, simplify, extract or modernize code.

remove-ai-slops.funcion: Removes AI-generated code smells behind regression tests.
remove-ai-slops.uso: Use it to clean up recent AI-generated changes.

review-work.funcion: Post-implementation gate review: real manual QA and a single control reviewer.
review-work.uso: Use it before handing off a PR or when asked to review completed work.

ultimate-browsing.funcion: Renders, drives and captures web pages, including WAF-blocked hosts.
ultimate-browsing.uso: Use it for JS-rendered sources, persistent logins and screenshots as proof.

ulw-execute.funcion: Executes a written work plan with state, an evidence ledger and parallel subagents.
ulw-execute.uso: Use it when asked to run a plan saved under .omo/plans.

ulw-plan.funcion: Planning consultant that writes one complete work plan before coding.
ulw-plan.uso: Use it only when the ulw-plan workflow or a pre-implementation plan is requested.

ulw-research.funcion: Maximum-saturation research with a cooperating team and a cited deliverable.
ulw-research.uso: Use it when research or a deep investigation is requested.

visual-qa.funcion: Rigorous visual QA across web, terminal and paginated surfaces, with screenshots and a verdict.
visual-qa.uso: Use it for any UI change or when asked whether something looks right.

defuddle.funcion: Extracts clean markdown from web pages, stripping clutter and navigation.
defuddle.uso: Use it instead of downloading a page when a URL is given to read, summarize or research.

github-public-writing.funcion: Writes or audits public GitHub repository content clearly.
github-public-writing.uso: Use it for READMEs, public documentation, compatibility tables and repository metadata.

json-canvas.funcion: Creates and edits JSON Canvas (.canvas) files with nodes, edges and groups.
json-canvas.uso: Use it for visual canvases, mind maps and diagrams that connect ideas.

juez-repo.funcion: Audits a GitHub repository the way a recruiter or potential client would see it.
juez-repo.uso: Use it when asked to audit the repository or check whether it is ready to show.

juez-tester.funcion: Diagnoses and fixes a problem, or self-audits finished work before review.
juez-tester.uso: Use it when asked to repair and validate, or to return a self-audit before the audit.

obsidian-bases.funcion: Creates and edits Obsidian Bases (.base) with views, filters and formulas.
obsidian-bases.uso: Use it to organize notes into tables, cards or lists.

obsidian-cli.funcion: Operates Obsidian vaults from the CLI and supports plugin or theme development.
obsidian-cli.uso: Use it to read, create and search notes, tasks and properties in a vault.

obsidian-markdown.funcion: Creates and edits Markdown with Obsidian syntax.
obsidian-markdown.uso: Use it for wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties and tags.

obsidian-second-brain-audit.funcion: Audits a vault so it works as a linked second brain.
obsidian-second-brain-audit.uso: Use it when notes end up disconnected or the vault needs structure.

obsidian-vault-writing-rules.funcion: Enforces professional vault writing: no monoliths, with hierarchy and links.
obsidian-vault-writing-rules.uso: Use it in any task that creates or edits documentation inside a vault.

opencode-multi-auth-fix.funcion: Diagnoses account errors from the Codex multi-auth plugin.
opencode-multi-auth-fix.uso: Use it on messages such as no available accounts or an expired token.

prompt-master.funcion: Writes or improves copy-ready OpenCode prompts.
prompt-master.uso: Use it when asked for a prompt for an OpenCode agent or to improve an existing one.

skill-creator.funcion: Creates new skills, improves existing ones and measures their performance.
skill-creator.uso: Use it to create a skill from scratch, edit one or optimize its description.

team-mode.funcion: Runs a lead plus coordinated member sessions with shared tasks and messages.
team-mode.uso: Use it when the user asks for a team, several coordinated agents in parallel, or the /team-mode command.

tui-design.funcion: Designs, builds and reviews terminal user interfaces.
tui-design.uso: Use it to create panels, explorers or interactive terminal views.

rigel-v2:version.queHace: Prints the Rigel V2 product version.
rigel-v2:version.queToca: Read-only over the built version; it changes no state.

rigel-v2:get-local-version.queHace: Compares the running version with the published one.
rigel-v2:get-local-version.queToca: Reads the local and remote versions; it changes nothing.

rigel-v2:doctor.queHace: Runs Rigel V2 health diagnostics across four categories.
rigel-v2:doctor.queToca: Inspects system, configuration, tools and models; it does not alter state.

rigel-v2:install.queHace: Installs or refreshes the Rigel V2 surface for a platform.
rigel-v2:install.queToca: With --platform opencode it only refreshes the runtime inside the isolated laboratory (opencode-v2-lab); it refuses to move the install outside it and never touches your OpenCode V1. It is not the public route: that is script/agent/setup.sh plus rigel-v2-user-install.mjs install --version 1. The codex and native platforms delegate to their installers.

rigel-v2:uninstall.queHace: Uninstalls the Rigel V2 surface for a platform.
rigel-v2:uninstall.queToca: With --platform opencode it removes the isolated-laboratory runtime entry and deletes the staged runtime and activation state; it refuses when the config does not register that runtime and never touches your OpenCode V1. The codex and native platforms delegate to their uninstallers.

rigel-v2:ulw-loop.queHace: Resolves and prints the Codex ulw-loop component command.
rigel-v2:ulw-loop.queToca: It only resolves and prints the command; it does not run the loop.

rigel-v2:worktree-sweep.queHace: Sweeps obsolete git worktrees in a repository.
rigel-v2:worktree-sweep.queToca: By default it removes the merged-and-clean worktrees of the repository; --dry-run only reports. It never sweeps protected prefixes.

rigel-v2:boulder.queHace: Inspects Rigel V2 native boulder and continuity state.
rigel-v2:boulder.queToca: Reads and prints the persistent work state; it does not alter it.

rigel-v2:refresh-model-capabilities.queHace: Resolves the V2 host model catalog into a capabilities snapshot.
rigel-v2:refresh-model-capabilities.queToca: Reads the V2 host catalog and writes the snapshot into the isolated-laboratory Rigel state; it does not touch project code.

rigel-v2:ast-grep.queHace: Provisions the sg binary for the ast-grep skill.
rigel-v2:ast-grep.queToca: Downloads and places the sg binary; it does not touch project code.

omo:install.queHace: Installs and configures the parent Oh My OpenCode product with a wizard.
omo:install.queToca: Configures the parent product; it does not configure Oh My Rigel.

omo:setup.queHace: Interactive setup wizard for the parent product.
omo:setup.queToca: Configures the parent Oh My OpenCode product; it is not Oh My Rigel.

omo:doctor.queHace: Checks the health of the parent product installation.
omo:doctor.queToca: Inspects the parent installation and models; it does not change Oh My Rigel.

omo:get-local-version.queHace: Shows the installed parent version and checks for updates.
omo:get-local-version.queToca: Version read; it modifies no state.

omo:cleanup.queHace: Cleans the managed Codex Light state (cache and marketplace) and repairs project-local Codex artifacts.
omo:cleanup.queToca: Only accepts --platform codex; it does not uninstall OmO or Oh My Rigel and does not touch your OpenCode V1.

omo:refresh-model-capabilities.queHace: Refreshes the models.dev-based model capabilities snapshot.

omo:version.queHace: Shows the parent product version information.

omo:boulder.queHace: Shows boulder progress, elapsed time and per-task statistics.

omo:worktree-sweep.queHace: Reports and, with --apply, removes obsolete git worktrees.
omo:worktree-sweep.queToca: By default it only reports (dry-run); --apply removes and prunes. It never removes locked worktrees.

omo:ulw-loop.queToca: Runs the loop and writes its own state.

omo:mcp.queHace: Manages MCP: OAuth login, logout and status.
omo:mcp.queToca: Registers or revokes OAuth credentials for MCP servers.

slash:goal.queHace: Sets, shows, pauses, resumes or clears the session's persistent goal.

slash:refactor.queHace: Guided refactor with LSP, ast-grep, architecture analysis and verification.
slash:refactor.queToca: May edit project code, always with verification.

slash:ulw-execute.queHace: Runs an Atlas work session from a Prometheus plan.
slash:ulw-execute.queToca: Runs the plan; it may create worktrees and PRs.

slash:stop-continuation.queHace: Stops every continuation mechanism in the session.
slash:stop-continuation.queToca: Stops continuation loops, todos and boulder; it deletes no finished work.

slash:remove-ai-slops.queHace: Removes AI code smells from the branch changes and reviews them.

slash:handoff.queHace: Creates a context summary to continue in a new session.
slash:handoff.queToca: Produces a summary; it does not change code.

slash:hyperplan.queToca: Coordinates several team members to plan; it does not edit code.

slash:btw.queHace: Opens an ephemeral side conversation with the agent.
slash:btw.queToca: Creates an isolated side session; it does not touch the main thread.

slash:side.queToca: Same as the side conversation: an isolated session that leaves the main thread alone.

slash:mcp-oauth.queHace: Manages OAuth authorization login, status, and logout for an MCP server.
slash:mcp-oauth.queToca: Stores or removes OAuth tokens in host storage; it never prints them.
